# Quarterly supplier review - Quillfeather Print

Date: 2026-11-05
Present: Rosa (our procurement), Jim (our marketing), Neil (Quillfeather Print), Wen (Quillfeather Print)

**Rosa:** Welcome, both. Thanks for coming over. Did the train behave?

**Neil:** Forty minutes late. But we're here.

**Jim:** Nice jumper, Neil.

**Neil:** Christmas present from my mother-in-law. Thank you for noticing.

**Rosa:** Right. This is just our quarterly review, nothing contentious. I'd like to hear how things have gone from your side and then Jim has a few comments.

**Wen:** Thanks. From our side the main thing is delivery. Our average turnaround on your orders is now three working days, down from five in the summer.

**Rosa:** That's good to hear. We noticed. Jim, you've seen fewer late brochures?

**Jim:** Yes, none late since September. Really good.

**Neil:** Good. The other thing I have to tell you is a price change. From the first of January our prices go up by four percent across the board.

**Rosa:** Four percent. Is that firm?

**Neil:** It's firm. It's the paper cost and energy. We held it as long as we could.

**Rosa:** Understood. I'm not going to fight it, four is reasonable.

**Jim:** I'd have expected more, honestly.

**Wen:** Also, from the new year we are moving all your brochures onto a recycled stock as standard. Same weight, slightly different feel.

**Jim:** Does it affect the colour?

**Wen:** Slightly warmer. We'll send samples at some point.

**Jim:** Lovely.

**Rosa:** Then a couple of things from us. October's invoices. There were errors on the batch from the middle of the month. Two invoices charged for the old rate.

**Neil:** Yes, I saw that. It's not fixed yet. Our accounts team are still looking at it.

**Rosa:** Okay, so it's still open on your side.

**Neil:** It's still open.

**Jim:** Should we, I don't know, look at a second supplier at some point? Just for resilience.

**Rosa:** We should probably think about it, yes. At some point. Not now.

**Neil:** I won't be offended.

**Rosa:** Ha, good. Somebody ought to check the contract renewal date too, I think it's in the spring.

**Jim:** I might email legal about that, though I've got a lot on.

**Rosa:** Only if you get a minute. Don't worry.

**Wen:** One more thing from us. There's talk of a paper shortage in the spring. The mills are cutting production and we may have trouble getting some stocks.

**Rosa:** How worried should we be?

**Wen:** If it happens, lead times could double on the heavier paper. It's not certain.

**Jim:** That would hurt the spring catalogue.

**Rosa:** Yes. Okay. Anything else?

**Neil:** I don't think so. The meeting room has a nice view, by the way.

**Rosa:** It's the only good thing about this building. Right, thanks everyone. We'll do the same again in February.

**Neil:** Same time. Safe travels, everyone.
